summary: Closed Phase 16 (Land the Anchor-Pointer Convention, Its Regression Lint, and a Pilot) [COMPLETED]. Landed context/standards/anchor-pointer-convention.md (new standard), a registry-driven regression lint (lint-anchor-pointer-collapse.sh, riding gate 9 -- no new gate row) with a 6-case fixture suite, and piloted the collapse on 5 agent files sharing early-metadata-pattern.md's re-derived top-sharing-factor eligible block (g=40, superseding the stale '68 files' Scope Hypothesis figure). Full claim-retention ledger recorded in the plan. Caught and fixed a real false-positive bug in the lint's own matching logic (grep -Fqz silently does an OR-of-single-lines match for a multi-line pattern, not contiguous substring containment) during this phase's own verification against the real repo -- replaced with bash's native [[ "$content" == *"$pattern"* ]]. Phase NET-MD: -31 (pilot -110, new standard +79); NET-PROD/NET-TEST net-positive this phase as a deliberate precondition for Phases 17-19's larger harvest. Full gate set run once: gate 9 PASSED (including the new lint); two unrelated findings (gate 8: 5 new-failing orchestrate/postflight suites; gate 10: a pre-existing TODO/state desync plus a host-load timeout), neither attributable to this phase's edits, recorded as issues rather than fixed (most plausibly concurrent sibling-dispatch contention on this shared repo). Also recorded: a necessary file_scope-widening commit swept in 3 unrelated-but-verified-correct pre-existing line_count corrections from the same shared file. 4 of 20 plan phases remain: 17-19 (markdown tranches A/B/C, already authorized for semantic rather than merely literal-text anchor-finding per the Phase-15 user_decision answered in a prior cycle) and 20 (redeploy, full gate set, measured net accounting).
